searchText: I would not disagree with the 2 approaches framework, neither. Based on what I gathered through various discussions, the middle approach has had the most mindshare. A lot of folks automatically assume that there will be a libp2p based networking layer for the light client. If we could make portal network to function as designed, that would be the best case scenario. Approach 1 of explicitly setting an RPC endpoint is by far the easiest to implement. hmm For the p2p approach, the main challenge is nailing down exactly what messages get passed around the network Whereas in the N-server approach, it's a much simpler "client asks for what they need, all servers respond" situation So one question for the p2p approach is, do we start immediately standardizing it as part of the portal network, or does it live as a separate network first and then we figure out how to incorporate it into portal later? Is that the choice there?
